angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 596,911 km at 90.93 pc = 0.09 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 10.9969 +/- 0.0116 mas (same row, RUWE 1.08): 90.93 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.858 +/- 0.032 solar radii from Hoyer et al. 2021, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-220 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021MNRAS.505.3361H/abstract): 596,911 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.825 +/- 0.028 solar masses from Hoyer et al. 2021, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-220 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021MNRAS.505.3361H/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5298 +/- 65 K from Hoyer et al. 2021, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-220 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021MNRAS.505.3361H/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Hoyer et al. 2021, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-220 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021MNRAS.505.3361H/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-220.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.488, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
